ei.title: Why Fashion Needs to Be More Sustainable
ei.subject: 공통영어1

fullPassage:
Why Fashion Needs to Be More Sustainable

Jessi is a fashion blogger who loves unique, vibrant clothes. But guess what? She does not buy new clothes. Instead, she buys them secondhand. You may think secondhand clothes are old-fashioned, but by buying them, Jessi can try different styles. She also does not get too attached to any style or brand because there is always another exciting outfit waiting to be discovered. Jessi's clothing habits are not just about creating a style; they are about saving the Earth. The reason is that her actions help reduce the production and consumption of clothes.

Worth over $3 trillion and making up 2% of the world's GDP, the fashion industry today has an almost entirely linear approach. The process moves in a straight line from design to consumption to disposal. Material extraction, textile manufacturing, the supply chain, design, sales, marketing, and other steps are guided by the aim of maximizing garment consumption without considering other issues. Due to linear fashion, the fashion industry negatively affects the environment. 85% of textiles go into landfills, only 1% of the materials is recycled, at least 500,000 tons of microfibers end up in the ocean (equal to 50 billion plastic bottles), and 93 billion cubic meters of water is required for textile production annually. Alarming numbers like these will keep increasing if producers maintain the old system. It is clear that waste and pollution from the fashion industry must be reduced. Linear fashion must change, and this could happen through circular fashion.

Circular fashion is inspired by the principles of a circular economy and sustainable development. A circular economy is based on limiting waste, keeping resources and materials in use, and reusing them. In a circular model, we make, use, and reuse materials for as long as possible to extract their maximum value. Therefore, clothing and textiles are produced, used, and reused to minimize waste. It is a renewable approach to reduce the fashion industry's environmental impact. Circular fashion provides numerous benefits. First, extending the lifespan of fibers significantly reduces textile waste, benefiting the environment. Second, circular processes utilize chemicals and materials safe for human health and the environment. This practice protects the environment and consumer health. Third, materials are regenerated instead of being disposed of, which enables their long-term use.

The rise of circular fashion is facilitated by new technology and ideas. Materials commonly used in clothing are not eco-friendly because they require considerable resources and often break down slowly. This creates a need for eco-friendly textile alternatives. Currently, companies are developing recycled fibers and fibers extracted from agricultural waste products like leaves, peels, and seeds. One company uses nanotechnology to make soft material from orange peels. Another makes fabrics from kapok tree seeds. The trees grow well in poor soil without needing much water. These new fabrics produce less waste, last a long time, and break down easily.

In addition to these manufacturing techniques, technology will improve in such a way that it may become normal to produce clothes only when people order them. This "make-to-order" method will cost more, but then less money will be spent on maintaining offline stores. And 3D technology will enable people to see how clothes will fit online without trying them on in a store. In the long run, innovation in production and sales will facilitate sustainable fashion and considerably reduce material waste and logistics emissions.

Another key to making fashion sustainable is the consumer: us. If we want the fashion industry to adopt more sustainable practices, we must care about how clothes come to us. We should then demonstrate our concerns through what we buy. The market, of course, will respond. We can also reduce waste by discarding clothes responsibly. To be specific, we should buy only what we need and pass clothing on to someone who will wear it or to a thrift shop when discarding it.

Circular fashion will not solve every problem in the fashion industry overnight. However, small steps in the right direction are better than nothing. Keeping things in the supply chain for as many cycles as possible is really important. By making small changes to our clothing habits today, the fashion industry will gradually improve. After all, nothing is more fashionable than saving the planet.

questions.passage: Jessi is a fashion blogger who loves unique, vibrant clothes.  But guess what?  She does not buy new clothes.  Instead, she buys them secondhand. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① buying(사는 것) → 정상 / ② waited → waiting(기다리는) / ③ creating(만드는) → 정상 / ④ reduce(줄이다) → 정상.
det.analysis:
✅ ① buying: 전치사 by 뒤 동명사 — 정상.
❌ ② waited: 원문은 waiting. outfit이 발견되기를 '기다리는' 능동 의미이므로 현재분사(waiting) 필요. waited(과거분사)는 틀림. ←정답
✅ ③ creating: 전치사 about 뒤 동명사 — 정상.
✅ ④ reduce: help + 동사원형 — 정상.
det.tip: 명사를 수식하는 분사: 능동(~하는) → 현재분사(-ing), 수동(~된) → 과거분사(-ed).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① entirely(완전히) → 정상 / ② guided(이끌리는) → 정상 / ③ considered → considering(고려하는) / ④ affects(영향을 미치다) → 정상.
det.analysis:
✅ ① entirely: 형용사 linear를 수식하는 부사 — 정상.
✅ ② guided: are guided by — 수동태 정상.
❌ ③ considered: 원문은 considering. 전치사 without 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 필요. considered(과거분사)는 틀림. ←정답
✅ ④ affects: 주어 the fashion industry(단수) + 3인칭 단수 현재 — 정상.
det.tip: 전치사(without) 뒤 → 동명사(considering). 과거분사(considered)는 불가.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① limiting(제한하는) → 정상 / ② extending(연장하는) → 정상 / ③ reduce → reduces(줄인다) / ④ safe(안전한) → 정상.
det.analysis:
✅ ① limiting: 전치사 on 뒤 동명사, limiting/keeping/reusing 병렬 — 정상.
✅ ② extending: 동명사 주어(extending the lifespan) — 정상.
❌ ③ reduce: 원문은 reduces. 동명사 주어 extending은 단수 취급이므로 단수동사 reduces 필요. reduce(원형)는 틀림. ←정답
✅ ④ safe: materials safe for — 형용사 후치수식 정상.
det.tip: 동명사 주어(~ing)는 단수 취급 → 단수동사(reduces).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① commonly(흔히) → 정상 / ② extracted(추출된) → 정상 / ③ needing(필요로 하는) → 정상 / ④ producing → to produce(생산하다).
det.analysis:
✅ ① commonly: 과거분사 used를 수식하는 부사 — 정상.
✅ ② extracted: fibers extracted from — 과거분사의 후치수식(추출된 섬유) 정상.

❌ ④ producing: 원문은 to produce. 'become normal to V' 구문에서 to부정사가 필요. producing(동명사)은 틀림. ←정답
det.tip: It is/becomes normal to V → to부정사 필수. 가주어 it 구문.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 극대화하는. 감소하는. 줄여야 한다. 순환.
det.analysis:
✅ ① maximizing: 의류 소비를 극대화(maximizing garment consumption) — 원문 그대로.
❌ ② decreasing: 원문은 increasing. 생산자가 오래된 시스템을 유지하면 놀라운 수치가 계속 '증가'해야 문맥상 맞음. decreasing(감소)은 문맥 반대. ←정답
✅ ③ reduced: waste and pollution must be reduced — 원문 그대로.
✅ ④ circular: through circular fashion — 원문 그대로.
det.tip: increasing(증가) ↔ decreasing(감소). 오래된 시스템 유지 → 수치 증가.

questions.passage: The rise of circular fashion is ①<u>hindered</u> by new technology and ideas.  Materials commonly used in clothing are not eco-friendly because they require ②<u>considerable</u> resources and often break down slowly.  This creates a need for eco-friendly textile alternatives.  Currently, companies are developing recycled fibers and fibers extracted from agricultural waste products like leaves, peels, and seeds.  One company uses nanotechnology to make soft material from orange peels.  Another makes fabrics from kapok tree seeds.  The trees grow well in ③<u>poor</u> soil without needing much water. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 방해되는. 상당한. 척박한. 쉽게.
det.analysis:
❌ ① hindered: 원문은 facilitated. 순환 패션의 부상은 새 기술에 의해 '촉진된다'가 맞음. hindered(방해된다)는 문맥 반대. ←정답
✅ ② considerable: require considerable resources — 원문 그대로.
✅ ③ poor: grow well in poor soil — 원문 그대로.
✅ ④ easily: break down easily — 원문 그대로.
det.tip: facilitated(촉진된) ↔ hindered(방해된).

det.korean: but by buying them, Jessi can try different styles.
det.analysis: ✅ T ←정답: 중고 옷을 사면(by buying them) 다양한 스타일을 시도할 수 있다(can try different styles)고 원문에 명시.
det.tip: by buying them = 그것들을 구매함으로써.

questions.stem: 패션 산업에서 발생하는 초미세 섬유 중 50만 톤이 재활용되고 있다.

det.korean: at least 500,000 tons of microfibers end up in the ocean.
det.analysis: ✅ F ←정답: 50만 톤의 초미세 섬유는 '바다로 흘러 들어간다(end up in the ocean)'. 재활용되는 것이 아님.
det.tip: end up in the ocean = 바다에 결국 도달하다. recycled가 아님.

questions.stem: 현재 기업들은 잎, 껍질, 씨앗 같은 농업 폐기물에서 섬유를 추출하여 개발하고 있다.

det.korean: companies are developing recycled fibers and fibers extracted from agricultural waste products like leaves, peels, and seeds.
det.analysis: ✅ T ←정답: 기업들이 농업 폐기물(agricultural waste products)인 잎, 껍질, 씨앗에서 추출된 섬유를 개발 중이라고 원문에 명시.
det.tip: extracted from agricultural waste products = 농업 폐기물에서 추출된.

questions.passage: Circular fashion is inspired by the principles of a circular economy and sustainable development.  A circular economy is based on limiting waste, keeping resources and materials in use, and reusing them.  In a circular model, we make, use, and reuse materials for as long as possible to extract their maximum value.  Therefore, clothing and textiles are produced, used, and reused to minimize waste.  It is a ______ approach to reduce the fashion industry's environmental impact.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 재생 가능한 접근 방식.
det.analysis:
❌ ① disposable(일회용의): 순환 패션은 폐기물을 최소화하는 것이 목적이므로 일회용 접근은 문맥 반대.
❌ ② linear(선형적인): 선형 패션은 이전 단락에서 문제로 제기된 방식. 순환 패션의 특성이 아님.
❌ ③ temporary(일시적인): 순환 모델은 재료를 가능한 한 오래 사용하는 것이므로 일시적과 반대.
✅ ④ renewable(재생 가능한): 원문 그대로. 폐기물 최소화 + 재사용 → 재생 가능한 접근 방식. ←정답
det.tip: renewable = 재생 가능한. 순환 경제의 핵심 가치.

questions.passage: Another key to making fashion sustainable is the consumer: us.  If we want the fashion industry to adopt more sustainable practices, we must care about how clothes come to us.  We should then ______ our concerns through what we buy.  The market, of course, will respond.  We can also reduce waste by discarding clothes responsibly.  To be specific, we should buy only what we need and pass clothing on to someone who will wear it or to a thrift shop when discarding it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 관심을 보여주다. 구매를 통해 우리의 우려를 드러내야 한다는 문맥.
det.analysis:
✅ ① demonstrate(보여주다): 원문 그대로. 구매 행위를 통해 관심을 '보여주어야 한다'는 문맥에 부합. ←정답
❌ ② suppress(억누르다): 관심을 억누르면 시장이 반응할 수 없음. 문맥 반대.
❌ ③ abandon(포기하다): 관심을 포기하라는 문맥이 아님.
❌ ④ postpone(미루다): 관심을 미루는 것은 본문 취지(적극적 소비자 행동)에 반함.
det.tip: demonstrate = 보여주다, 증명하다. concerns = 관심, 우려.

A circular economy is based on limiting waste, keeping resources and materials in use, and reusing them.  In a circular model, we make, use, and reuse materials for as long as possible to extract their maximum value.  Therefore, clothing and textiles are produced, used, and reused to minimize waste.  It is a renewable approach to reduce the fashion industry's environmental impact.  Circular fashion provides numerous benefits.  First, extending the lifespan of fibers significantly reduces textile waste, benefiting the environment.  Second, circular processes utilize chemicals and materials safe for human health and the environment.  This practice protects the environment and consumer health.  Third, materials are regenerated instead of being disposed of, which enables their long-term use.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ① 재료 재생. ② 화학물질 유해. ③ 폐기물 증가. ④ 일회용 권장.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 순환 패션에서 재료는 폐기 대신 재생된다. — materials are regenerated instead of being disposed of. 원문 일치. ←정답
❌ ② 순환 과정의 화학 물질은 인체에 해롭다. — chemicals and materials safe for human health. 안전하다고 했으므로 불일치.
❌ ③ 섬유 수명 연장은 직물 폐기물을 증가시킨다. — significantly reduces textile waste. 줄인다고 했으므로 불일치.
❌ ④ 순환 경제는 자원의 일회용 사용을 권장한다. — reusing them. 재사용을 권장하므로 불일치.
det.tip: regenerated = 재생된. disposed of = 폐기된.

ch: 순환 패션에서 재료는 폐기 대신 재생된다.
순환 과정에서 사용되는 화학 물질은 인체에 해롭다.
섬유의 수명을 연장하면 직물 폐기물이 증가한다.
순환 경제는 자원의 일회용 사용을 권장한다.

questions.passage:
These new fabrics produce less waste, last a long time, and break down easily.

In addition to these manufacturing techniques, technology will improve in such a way that it may become normal to produce clothes only when people order them.  This "make-to-order" method will cost more, but then less money will be spent on maintaining offline stores. In the long run, innovation in production and sales will facilitate sustainable fashion and considerably reduce material waste and logistics emissions.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ① 비용 증가. ② 매장비 절감. ③ 물류 배출 감소. ④ 3D 매장 필수.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 주문 제작 방식은 비용이 더 들 것이다. — will cost more. 원문 일치.
❌ ② 오프라인 매장 유지 비용이 줄어들 것이다. — less money will be spent on maintaining offline stores. 원문 일치.
❌ ③ 생산과 판매의 혁신은 물류 배출을 상당히 줄일 것이다. — considerably reduce material waste and logistics emissions. 원문 일치.
✅ ④ 3D 기술은 매장에서 직접 옷을 입어 봐야만 활용할 수 있다. — without trying them on in a store. 매장에서 입어보지 '않고도' 가능하므로 불일치. ←정답
det.tip: without trying them on = 입어보지 않고도. 매장 방문 불필요.

ch: 주문 제작 방식은 비용이 더 들 것이다.
오프라인 매장 유지 비용이 줄어들 것이다.
생산과 판매의 혁신은 물류 배출을 상당히 줄일 것이다.
3D 기술은 매장에서 직접 옷을 입어 봐야만 활용할 수 있다.

questions.passage:
Jessi is a fashion blogger who loves unique, vibrant clothes.  But guess what?  She does not buy new clothes.  Instead, she buys them secondhand.  Jessi's clothing habits are not just about creating a style; they are about saving the Earth.  The reason is that her actions help reduce the production and consumption of clothes.

Worth over $3 trillion and making up 2% of the world's GDP, the fashion industry today has an almost entirely linear approach.  Due to linear fashion, the fashion industry negatively affects the environment.  It is clear that waste and pollution from the fashion industry must be reduced.  Linear fashion must change, and this could happen through circular fashion.

Circular fashion is inspired by the principles of a circular economy and sustainable development.  A circular economy is based on limiting waste, keeping resources and materials in use, and reusing them.  Therefore, clothing and textiles are produced, used, and reused to minimize waste.  It is a renewable approach to reduce the fashion industry's environmental impact.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 전체 주제: 순환 패션의 필요성.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 중고 의류 시장의 경제적 가치와 성장 가능성 — 제시의 중고 소비는 도입부 예시일 뿐, 전체 주제 아님.
✅ ② 패션 산업의 환경 문제 해결을 위한 순환 패션의 필요성 ←정답: 선형 패션의 환경 문제 → 순환 패션으로 전환 필요.
❌ ③ 섬유 제조 과정에서 발생하는 화학 물질의 위험성 — 화학 물질 위험성은 본문 주제 아님.
❌ ④ 3D 기술이 패션 산업의 미래에 미치는 영향 — 3D 기술은 일부 사례일 뿐.
det.tip: 제목: Why Fashion Needs to Be More Sustainable.

questions.passage:
Another key to making fashion sustainable is the consumer: us.  If we want the fashion industry to adopt more sustainable practices, we must care about how clothes come to us.  We should then demonstrate our concerns through what we buy.  The market, of course, will respond.  We can also reduce waste by discarding clothes responsibly.  To be specific, we should buy only what we need and pass clothing on to someone who will wear it or to a thrift shop when discarding it.

Circular fashion will not solve every problem in the fashion industry overnight.  However, small steps in the right direction are better than nothing.  Keeping things in the supply chain for as many cycles as possible is really important.  By making small changes to our clothing habits today, the fashion industry will gradually improve.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 소비자의 의식적 소비가 패션 산업 변화를 이끈다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 기술 혁신만으로 패션 산업의 모든 문제를 해결할 수 있다. — 소비자 역할 강조 문단이므로 기술만으로 해결 가능하다는 주장 아님.
❌ ② 소비자는 옷을 최대한 많이 구매하여 경제를 활성화해야 한다. — buy only what we need. 필요한 것만 사라고 했으므로 반대.
✅ ③ 소비자의 의식적인 구매와 책임 있는 폐기가 지속 가능한 패션에 기여한다. ←정답: demonstrate our concerns through what we buy + discarding clothes responsibly.
❌ ④ 중고품 가게는 환경 보호에 실질적인 도움이 되지 않는다. — pass clothing on to a thrift shop. 중고품 가게 활용을 권장하므로 반대.
det.tip: 요지 = 소비자가 구매와 폐기를 통해 변화를 이끌 수 있다.

ch: 기술 혁신만으로 패션 산업의 모든 문제를 해결할 수 있다.
소비자는 옷을 최대한 많이 구매하여 경제를 활성화해야 한다.
소비자의 의식적인 구매와 책임 있는 폐기가 지속 가능한 패션에 기여한다.
중고품 가게는 환경 보호에 실질적인 도움이 되지 않는다.
